subject: Re: estimating abundance of juvenile chinook in pools in an

messages.author: 38d2d456a5eb32ab
messages.subject: Re: estimating abundance of juvenile chinook in pools in an
parts:
hi Eric. thank you for your response to my questions. i wonder if i
could ask a few follow-up questions?

On Wed, Jun 11, 2008 at 1:26 AM, Eric Rexstad <er...@mcs.st-and.ac.uk> wrote:

> > when doing point transect sampling rather than line transect sampling. You
> > dismiss transect sampling because fish aggregate around CWD. I would
> > reconsider that decision, as the population you are sampling are the
> > individuals in the pool, not individuals at CWD in the pool; so you ought to
> > be diligent about sampling the population of interest to you, rather than
> > only the high density area.

the reason i think a transect won't work is because it would be very
hard to move the camera along a line in a big pile of wood (we would
have to be continuously taking it in and out of the water and
adjusting angles and disturbing fish repeatedly), while if we sample
at points on a grid or at randomly selected points it would reduce the
amount of maneuvering required to place the camera, and let us put it
in, give the fish a minute to settle, and count fish and measure
distances on 1 frame 1 minute into the video for each point. i'm not
planning to avoid sampling in any given place, just thinking about the
logistics of sampling on points v. sampling on lines. make sense?

> > If you employ the point transect sampling approach you've described here,
> > you will need to adjust your sampling effort to take account of the cameras
> > always facing upstream (so you're really not making detections 360-degrees
> > around the pole on which the camera is mounted (see p.55 of Buckland et al.
> > (2001)).

understood.

> > You don't have a choice of not estimating cluster size. If you don't
> > estimate cluster size, you will only produce an estimate of the density of
> > clusters in your pools; and that's not very biologically informative. Your

what i was actually wondering is whether using a cluster estimation is
a better approach than just counting individual fish as though they
were not clustered? they do aggregate, but often quite loosely or not
at all. or maybe this trait just makes them bad candidates for
distance sampling methods?


> > comment about 'missing the mother load in the pool' suggests you need to
> > adequately sample the pool (sufficient number of points, or transects). No
> > real surprise there. If you're using cameras, are you recording (taping)

is there any rule of thumb about what percentage of the area should
actually be sampled? the guidelines in the book refer more to numbers
of individuals than to a proportion of the space you are drawing
inferences on. but i could reasonably imagine a scenario where the
random sampling effort required to see 100 fish missed entirely the
major cluster of fish in the pool.

> > The driving factor behind this decision is producing an adequate sample of
> > the population of interest to you. If you lay a 1x1 grid onto your pool
> > (which seems quite labourious in and of itself), you could employ that grid
> > to take a systematic random sample (which will provide you with better
> > spatial coverage of your pool than pure random sampling). But there must
> > remain a random component of your sampling; if you are visiting each 1x1
> > grid cell, then place the camera in the centre of each of them; do not try
> > to select somewhere within the cell with the most fish or the best clarity
> > (that's not really random sampling).

that's what i thought. but it has been suggested that it is wasted
effort and violates common sense to put the camera, say, at a randomly
selected point where your view is obstructed by a big log, rather than
20 cm over where you can see. but i've been thinking this is the
purpose of calculating detectability anyway?

> > the pool. You seem to suggest that the pool's geometry will change over
> > time (in the most extreme drought case, a previous sampling site may be
> > beach by July before the Fairbanks monsoons start). My opinion is that your
> > 10x3m pool sampling area may need to change during the summer.

great! thanks.

i really appreciate your input. thank you.

bessie
